key_insight: Quantum cost landscapes often contain low-cost ravines, and exploiting these paths lets ensembles of quantum neural networks make better predictions with less optimization effort.
engineering_relevance: For variational quantum algorithms, ravine-aware ensembling can improve accuracy and convergence while cutting compute versus naive multi-model training.
method: Adapted the nudged elastic band (NEB) algorithm to trace low-cost paths between local minima in quantum cost landscapes.
Trained quantum neural networks to classify concentratable entanglement and probed hardware-efficient ansatz landscapes.
Built an ensemble by averaging predictions from models sampled along the NEB ravine path; introduced a lightweight local-prediction-variability metric.
evidence_signal: Across circuit and weight initializations with high local-prediction variability, the NEB-based quantum ensembles outperformed classical and naive quantum baselines, and scaling tests showed ravines persist with better convergence than naive ensembling.
watch_item: The approach depends on identifying ravine structure and may require extra NEB/path-finding overhead, so benefits could diminish when landscapes are not strongly ravine-like.
paper_title: Ravines in quantum cost landscapes: opportunities for improved VQA predictions
